what_went_well: You picked factorisation straight away, which is a sensible method for this quadratic, and you carried it out cleanly: (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0 in Step 2 is a correct factorisation of x^2 - 5x + 6. In Step 3 you set each bracket to zero and read off both roots, x = 2 and x = 3, so nothing was lost along the way. Full marks on all four criteria for a total of 6/6.
what_went_wrong: Nothing went wrong here — there is no step in your working that cost you a mark. The only thing I would flag is presentational: Step 3 jumps from the product form to the two roots without writing down the intermediate lines x - 2 = 0 and x - 3 = 0. The marker could see your reasoning this time, but on a harder question that gap is where method marks go missing.
how_to_improve: On your next factorising question, write the two sub-equations x - 2 = 0 and x - 3 = 0 as their own line before stating the roots, so the zero-product step is visible rather than implied. Then expand your brackets back out in the margin and check you recover x^2 - 5x + 6 before you go on. Both habits take a few seconds and protect the method marks when the numbers get uglier.
